text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria is expected to harvest 3.2 millions tonnes of wheat this year, up from the 1.8 million tonnes it needs to cover domestic consumption, head of Wheat and Sunflower Institute Ivan Panayotov said. @
-- Electricity prices are expected to rise by seven percent and central heating prices by 12-15 percent from July 1 under proposals by the National Electricity Company and the Energy Commitee.
-- Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov postponed his visit to Turkey scheduled for this week until after the formation of a new government in Ankara, the presidency said. @
-- Prices of imported cigarettes are expected to fall by 15 percent due to the stable lev under a Trade Ministry proposal to be discussed at a cabinet meeting today.

-- The Union for National Salvation, formed by ethnic turks and monarchists and one of the smaller parties in parliament, said it would seek a parliamentary investigation into the former socialist government of Zhan Videnov which they said had led the country to its current severe economic crisis. @

-- Bulgaria will open the archives of the former Politbureau, the top ruling body of the Communist Party which was in power for 45 years until November 1989, State Administration Minister Mario Tagarinski said.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to approve today draft amendments to the Penal Code as part of its programme to fight organised crime and corruption.
-- Some 30 percent of the staff of the cash-strapped Bulgarian National Television will be laid off in September as a part of a restructuring programme aimed to cut losses. @

-- Multinational naval exercises Cooperative Partner 97 began in Bulgarian territorial waters of the Black Sea on Sunday, as part of the Partnership for Peace programme. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
